kuvaus.en:
Do you want to study in a leading research environment at the University of Oulu? The Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) degree programme at the University of Oulu prepares future Diploma Engineers (M.Sc. in Technology) to develop innovative software, intelligent systems, and secure digital solutions that address complex societal and industrial challenges.

Digitalization, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and data-driven decision-making are transforming every sector of society. Therefore, the demand for highly skilled Computer Science and Engineering professionals continues to grow.

In CSE degree programme, you will acquire a strong foundation in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, computer science, software engineering, cloud computing, robotics, and human-centred digital technologies.

By combining world-class research, close collaboration with industry, and an international learning environment, the University of Oulu's Computer Science and Engineering degree programme provides you with the knowledge, practical skills, and innovative mindset needed to build successful a career and create technologies that shape the future of Finland and the world.

osaamistavoitteet.en:
The Degree Programme in Computer Science and Engineering focuses on providing a wide range of skills and knowledge needed in research, product development, and production of computer-based devices, services and systems including, for example, expertise for developing solutions to artificial intelligence based data analysis, Internet of Things, interactive systems and cyber security. The programme is based on the latest research excellence and prepares students to apply their skills in working life, and gives them tools for continuous learning as well.

After completing the BSc studies you

  • know the essential concepts, methods, and technologies in computer science and engineering
  • can use and apply the acquired knowledge in a creative and critical manner in your work
  • are able to work responsibly both independently and as a team member
  • can use information technology tools and communication skills in your work
  • can follow and interpret developments in computer science and engineering and develop your own study skills and knowledge
  • can communicate independently in your mother tongue, as well as in the second official language and at least in one foreign language to an international audience
  • are able to express technical matters both literally and verbally.

After completing the MSc studies you

  • can work as an expert of computer science and engineering in international communities
  • master profoundly and diversely the concepts, theory, and methods related to the selected orientation, and know the basics in the fields of the complementary and optional studies
  • can apply the acquired knowledge in a creative manner in research, development and management
  • master the communication and collaboration skills needed in working life
  • can conduct scientific research and create new knowledge for the needs of the companies and the society
  • have the abilities required for postgraduate studies and continuous professional development.

After completing the degree, you will also achieve the common generic skills of the University of Oulu, which are described on the Common generic skills and learning outcomes of the degrees page.

Specialization-specific learning outcomes:

Applied Computing

After completing the bachelor's degree, you are familiar with digital technologies and approaches that enhance everyday life (VR/XR, IoT, and HCI), know how to use collaborative development tools like Git, and can utilize various engines and frameworks to develop applications on different platforms. A human-centered perspective plays an important role. After completing the master's degree, you have a broad understanding of various fields of applied computing and the ability to build complex systems using different technologies in both physical and virtual environments.

Artificial Intelligence

After completion of the bachelor's degree, you understand the basics of machine learning and artificial intelligence. After completion of the master's degree, you master AI solutions, including machine learning methods, the processing of various data sources and signals, as well as data analysis and data-driven reasoning, and can apply these methods in areas such as computer vision, speech recognition, and data mining.

Computer Engineering

After completion of the bachelor's degree, you have a comprehensive basic knowledge and skills related to the hardware, processors, software, signal processing, lifecycles, and security of embedded systems. After completion of the master's degree, you have an in-depth understanding of Internet of Things (IoT) applications and physical devices, as well as low-power implementations.

Cyber Security

After completion of the bachelor's degree, you have a broad understanding of the basics and phenomena of the cybersecurity field. You have good basic skills in cybersecurity testing including other necessary technical skills and are prepared to further educate themselves for various tasks in the cybersecurity field. After completion of the master's degree, you have an in-depth understanding of the phenomena and field of cybersecurity, have specialized in a specific area of cybersecurity, and have extensive knowledge of the cybersecurity of software, devices, networks, and cloud services.

teksti.en:
The Computer Science and Engineering degree programme comprises 300 ECTS credits, including bachelor's studies (180 ECTS credits) and master's studies (120 ECTS credits).

The BSc studies in CSE consists of orientation, language and communication studies, courses on mathematics and natural sciences that build a basis for professional studies, major studies, and a supplementary module. Optional studies can be selected from entrepreneurship, economy, information processing science, or electrical engineering.

The MSc studies in CSE provide students with broad expertise, as well as skills and competencies needed for a wide range of professional roles in the field of ICT. The study option is selected from Artificial Intelligence, Applied Computing, Embedded Systems and Cyber Security. Furthermore, advanced and supplementary modules are available.

A student can choose the specialization based on their interests, for example, in intelligent systems and techniques like artificial intelligence and digital signal processing. They can also focus on designing embedded systems for smart phones, mobile base stations, cars, and wearable devices. Or they can train to become a specialist who masters the new technologies such as Internet of Things and human-centered computing and can develop new software and devices to meet the needs identified by users and businesses. Additionally, they can examine research, application and product development tasks of devices and software from a cyber security perspective.

A wide range of teaching methods is used throughout the programme. In addition to lectures and exercises, the studies include laboratory work, independent studying, project work, and group assignments. Many courses are offered through online or blended teaching but studying in the degree programme also requires attendance on the University of Oulu campus.

A student selects one of the four orientations during the Spring of the 2nd year:

  • Artificial Intelligence
  • Applied Computing
  • Computer Engineering
  • Cyber Security

The preparatory module of the orientation is included in the BSc studies, and the basic module and the advanced module of the orientation in the MSc studies.

Applied Computing focuses on the next generation of interactive systems that place humans at the focus of the technological development. Adopting a multidisciplinary real-world approach, students have to spend a substantial amount of time working in group projects to develop a variety of systems ranging from interactive online services to games and mobile applications, with a strong focus on innovation and design.

Artificial Intelligence focuses on various fields of AI such as machine learning, machine vision and data mining. This specialization provides students with a solid theoretical understanding and practical skills on processing and analyzing digital data and the ability to create intelligent solutions to real world problems with modern AI techniques.

Computer Engineering focuses on both hardware and software aspects of computing. In this specialization, students also study signal processing and its applications, and work with projects on modern signal processors and embedded computers. The specialization gives the students a good basis to work with Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

Cyber Security covers various aspects about modern information security such as possible vulnerabilities, attack vectors and preventive methods in user, software and hardware level. The focus is on hands-on exercises and project work with good theoretical understanding of the topics.

In addition, the student selects a supplementary module and optional courses both for BSc and MSc studies to fulfill the requirements of the degree.

As a graduate of the Computer Science and Engineering degree programme, you will be equipped to work in a wide range of expert and leadership roles across the public and private sectors.

Typical career paths include software engineer, AI engineer, machine learning specialist, data scientist, cybersecurity expert, cloud solutions architect, systems engineer, research and development engineer, product manager, technology consultant, entrepreneur and researcher.

As you gain more work experience, you may also progress into leadership roles in technology management, business development and international expert organizations.

The University of Oulu Study Guide for the next academic year will be published in February. Once the Study Guide has been published, you can find the latest degree structure of the programme, including the courses required for the degree, as follows: Go to the Study Guide. Select the upcoming academic year from the academic year menu. Then select the desired level of education (for example, bachelor's programmes, master's programmes, or doctoral programmes), after which you can choose the faculty and programme you are interested in.​

The bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering includes a BSc thesis (8 ECTS cr), which is made independently or as a group work. In addition, the BSc thesis includes technical communication studies (2 ECTS cr).

The master’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering includes an MSc thesis (30 ECTS cr), which is made independently and often as a work commissioned by an external customer such as a company from a topic related to its research or product development. The MSc thesis can be also made in the university research unit when it is more focused on scientific work and its documentation.

To be awarded a bachelor’s and master's degree, a student must complete the required studies and the thesis, write a maturity essay demonstrating language proficiency in the language in which the student has been educated (Finnish or Swedish). The student shall demonstrate the satisfactory level of proficiency in Finnish and Swedish required in the Act (424/2003) section 6 subsection 1. A student who has already demonstrated his/her language proficiency for a lower university degree (Bachelor) does not, however, need to demonstrate it again for a master´s degree. The diploma for the degrees of Bachelor of Science and Master of Science (Diploma Engineer) is awarded on request and issued by the Education Dean of the Faculty.

Teaching and research personnel in the Degree Programme in Computer Science and Engineering constantly and closely collaborate with companies in various projects, which gives a good basis for taking into account the requirements from the working life in teaching. For example, external specialists from companies can provide practical aspects to the topics addressed in courses. Studies include also several courses where project work is practiced along with collaboration and communication skills that are essential in working life. The students can include a supplementary module on working life and entrepreneurship in their BSc studies as well as practical training. The BSc thesis can be made on a topic defined by a company. In order to guarantee that the graduates have some  basic level of work experience from the field, MSc studies include compulsory practical training in a company, research institute or university. In addition, many companies hire students to make an MSc thesis, which gives them an opportunity to integrate to the working life already during their studies.

Computer Science and Engineering is one of the most international fields in the University of Oulu. A significant part of the personnel consists of foreign teachers and researchers. English is the teaching language in some of the BSc level courses and mainly in the MSc studies, where students are in the same groups with the exchange and international master’s degree students. The degree programme has several exchange agreements with foreign universities that give a good opportunity for the students to go to exchange during the BSc and MSc studies. Companies in the field of computer science and engineering are typically international or multinational having sites in several countries and operating in international markets. Hence, the MSc theses, for example, are commonly  written in English.

The Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering is a highly international and multidisciplinary academic community. The Faculty conducts both fundamental research and applied research that serves the needs of society and industry.

The Computer Science Research Unit conducts world-class research in machine vision, biomedical engineering, intelligent information analysis, cybersecurity, robotics, and virtual reality. These research areas are also strongly represented in the education provided by the Computer Science degree programme. Research groups frequently hire students as interns and MSc thesis workers, providing an excellent opportunity to continue as a doctoral researcher after graduation, pursue a doctoral degree, and build a career in research.

Research in computer science ranges from theoretically oriented topics to highly practical projects carried out in close collaboration with industry. Research projects are funded, for example, by Business Finland, the Research Council of Finland, the European Commission, various foundations, and industry.

For more information about research, visit the websites of the research groups within the CSE research unit:

Biomimetics and Intelligent Systems

Centre for Machine Vision and Signal Analysis

Centre for Applied Computing
The Master’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering gives a qualification for doctoral studies.

  • A transcript of records​ which includes the courses on which the selection is based
  • Course descriptions and learning outcomes for courses completed elsewhere than at the University of Oulu
  • A proof of your English language skills. Applications without the proof of language skills will not proceed in student selection.​
  • A copy of passport or identity card if you are not Finnish citizen. If you are not a Finnish citizen but are exempt from paying tuition fees, please note that you must prove this by uploading a document that proves your status as a non-fee-paying applicant.

kuvaus.en:
The online application at Studyinfo.fi instructs if you must upload attachments to support your application.​

Applicants applying with a diploma completed outside Finland:​

  • A proof of your English language skills. Applications without the proof of language skills will not proceed in student selection.​
  • The upper secondary school or higher education degree certificate and academic transcript in original language. Official translations of degree certificate and transcript of records if they were issued in a language other than Finnish, Swedish, or English.​
  • A copy of passport or identity card if you are not Finnish citizen. If you are not a Finnish citizen but are exempt from paying tuition fees, please note that you must prove this by uploading a document that proves your status as a non-fee-paying applicant.​
  • SAT test results 
     

Most Finnish diplomas are available to universities through the national Studyinfo SUPA database (Suorituspalvelu). Information on your qualification is available in the database if you have already completed, or will complete in spring 2027, one of the following qualifications:

  • the Finnish matriculation examination in 1990 or later
  • a vocational upper secondary qualification in 2017 or later
  • a further vocational qualification, or a specialist vocational qualification in 2018 or later
  • a Finnish higher education degree in 2003 or later
  • the Deutsches Internationales Abitur diploma (DIA) in Finland in 2019 or later
  • the European Baccalaureate (EB) diploma in Finland in 2023 of later

More information regarding the required documents on the website of University of Oulu.
